- $ a - b - c + d = (a - c) - (b - d) = x - y $

$$

It is a known identity in real numbers that for any real $ x $ and $ y $,
$$
\max(|x + y|, |x - y|) = |x| + |y|
$$

This identity holds because the maximum of the two absolute values corresponds to the sum of their magnitudes when considering all possible sign combinations.

\sum_{a=0}^8 \sum_{b=0}^8 \sum_{c=0}^8 \sum_{d=0}^8 (|a - c| + |b - d|)
